ai.description: This small toad reaches 3–4 cm. It is yellowish-brown with dark brown mottling and a smooth, glandular belly. Key features include a blunt snout and a distinct, dark-edged pale stripe along the back.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Malabar Toad (*Firouzophrynus hololius*) is best distinguished by its smooth, unspotted belly and the absence of a cranial crest, unlike the warty, ridged common toads.
ai.habitat: The Malabar toad inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Malabar toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its terrestrial retreats after dark to forage for small invertebrates in humid forest environments.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Malabar Toad is an explosive breeder that spawns in temporary rain pools during the monsoon season (June–August), laying large clutches of eggs in gelatinous strings.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Malabar toad (*Firouzophrynus hololius*) is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Toad produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard emanating from rocky streams or crevices during the monsoon.
